newsitem.title: USA: Stocks higher in early trade, supported by bonds.
newsitem.headline: Stocks higher in early trade, supported by bonds.

text.p: Wall Street stocks, supported by a steady bond market, followed through on last week's late momentum and moved higher in early trading Monday.
The Dow Jones industrial average topped 50 points in early trading, and shortly after 10 a.m. EDT, the index was up 47.59 points at 6,573.66, after having gone as high as 6,581.
Advances led declining issues by 1,198 to 465.
The long bond was up 12/32 of a point, or $3.75 per $1,000 face value, and its yield slipped to 7.09 percent from 7.12 percent Friday.
High-tech issues resumed their rally and led the way higher.
"The bond market is bouncing, and the stock market is tagging along. It's a continuation of the move we saw Friday afternoon," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management.

"High-techs were the most oversold of all sectors, hence the bounce this morning isn't a great surprise," he said. "Volatility in the sector worked against it when the market was going down. It will work in their favour as the market moves higher."
Alex. Brown Inc. leaped 10-1/4 to 63-3/8 on news of its takeover by Bankers Trust New York Corp. Bankers Trust was down 1-7/8 at 80-3/8.
Cisco Systems Inc. was the most actively traded Nasdaq issue, up 2-1/4 at 53-1/8. It was followed by Intel Corp., up 2-18 at 1476-1/82.
